eras.name: Iron Age and the petty kingdoms
The Norwegian realm at its height

events.title: First settlers follow the retreating ice
events.description: Hunter-gatherers move up the newly ice-free coast, leaving the Fosna and Hensbacka tool assemblages on raised beaches from Rogaland to Finnmark.

events.title: Rock carvings begin at Alta
events.description: The first of thousands of figures are cut into the shoreline rock at Alta in Finnmark, a record that keeps being added to for four and a half thousand years.

events.title: Farming reaches the south
events.description: Cereal growing and stock keeping appear around the Oslofjord and in Rogaland, spreading slowly north where the growing season allows.

events.title: The Battle Axe culture arrives
events.description: Corded Ware groups spread into southern Norway with new burial customs and shaft-hole axes, part of the wider Indo-European movement into Scandinavia.

events.title: The Nordic Bronze Age
events.description: Metal reaches Norway through trade rather than local ore, and the rock art shifts from hunting scenes to ships, ploughs and sun symbols.

events.title: Ship carvings at Bardal and Begby
events.description: Long rowed vessels are cut into rock faces across the south, the earliest evidence of the hull tradition that eventually produces the Viking ship.

events.era_name: Iron Age and the petty kingdoms
events.title: Bog iron and the Pre-Roman Iron Age
events.description: Norwegians begin smelting iron from bog ore, which removes the dependence on imported metal and puts tools and weapons within reach of ordinary farms.

events.era_name: Iron Age and the petty kingdoms
events.title: Roman goods reach the fjords
events.description: Glass, bronze vessels and coins arrive through Danish and German intermediaries, concentrated in a small number of unusually rich graves.

events.era_name: Iron Age and the petty kingdoms
events.title: The earliest runic inscriptions
events.description: Short texts in the Elder Futhark appear on weapons and stones, the first written Norwegian and the start of a script used for a thousand years.

events.era_name: Iron Age and the petty kingdoms
events.title: Hillforts and the Migration Period
events.description: Hundreds of defended hilltop sites are built across the south, and grave goods suggest a warrior elite consolidating control over the farming districts.

events.era_name: Iron Age and the petty kingdoms
events.title: The dust veil and the Fimbulwinter
events.description: A volcanic dust veil darkens the northern hemisphere and crops fail for years. Something like a third of Norwegian farms are abandoned, and the catastrophe may sit behind the Norse memory of the Fimbulwinter.

events.era_name: Iron Age and the petty kingdoms
events.title: Petty kingdoms take shape
events.description: The written record and the grave evidence agree on a landscape of small realms - Vestfold, Trondelag, Hordaland, Rogaland - each a fjord system with a chieftain at its head.

events.era_name: Iron Age and the petty kingdoms
events.title: The trading town of Kaupang
events.description: A market settlement grows on the Vestfold shore with imported pottery, glass and Arab silver - Norway's first thing recognisable as a town.

events.title: The raid on Lindisfarne
events.description: Norse raiders sack the monastery on Lindisfarne. The attack shocks Christian Europe and is taken, by convention, as the opening of the Viking Age.

events.title: The Oseberg ship is built
events.description: A twenty-two metre oak vessel is built in Vestfold, carved along the prow and stern and light enough to be rowed or sailed.

events.title: Norse settle the Faroes
events.description: Farmers from western Norway take sheep and barley to the Faroe Islands, the first step of the North Atlantic expansion.

events.title: The Oseberg burial
events.description: Two women are buried in the Oseberg ship with a cart, sledges, textiles and fifteen horses - the richest Viking Age grave ever found in Scandinavia.

events.title: Norse ships reach Iceland
events.description: Norwegian sailors sight and then overwinter on Iceland. Within a lifetime the island is settled, largely from the western fjords.

events.title: Harald Fairhair wins at Hafrsfjord
events.description: The saga tradition has Harald Fairhair defeat a coalition of petty kings at Hafrsfjord and become the first king of a unified Norway. The date and the scale are both disputed, but the dynasty is real.

events.title: Ottar's voyage to the White Sea
events.description: A Norwegian chieftain describes his northern voyages to King Alfred of Wessex, giving the earliest written account of Norway and of the Sami who paid him tribute.

events.title: The Gokstad burial
events.description: A chieftain is buried in a heavier, sturdier ship than Oseberg, built for the open sea. A replica later crosses the Atlantic under sail.

events.title: Iceland founds the Althing
events.description: The Icelandic settlers - overwhelmingly of Norwegian descent - establish an annual assembly at Thingvellir rather than accept a king.

events.title: Erik Bloodaxe dies at Stainmore
events.description: The last Norse king of York, and a son of Harald Fairhair, is killed in northern England, closing Norwegian ambitions there for a century.

events.title: Erik the Red settles Greenland
events.description: Outlawed from Iceland, Erik the Red leads a colonising fleet to the south-western Greenland fjords, extending Norse settlement to a fourth landmass.

events.title: Olaf Tryggvason takes the throne
events.description: Baptised in England, Olaf returns and takes Norway by force, then imposes Christianity on the coastal districts by a mixture of preaching and mutilation.

events.title: Leif Erikson reaches Vinland
events.description: Sailing from Greenland, Leif Erikson lands in North America. A Norse site at L'Anse aux Meadows in Newfoundland confirms the sagas five centuries before Columbus.

events.title: The Battle of Svolder
events.description: Olaf Tryggvason is defeated at sea by a Danish-Swedish coalition and jumps overboard in full armour. Norway is partitioned between the victors.

events.title: Olaf Haraldsson returns
events.description: Olaf Haraldsson sails home from Normandy, defeats the Danish earls and rebuilds a single Norwegian kingdom with the church as its instrument.

events.title: Christian law at Moster
events.description: An assembly at Moster adopts a Christian law code for the realm - the moment Norway becomes formally, rather than nominally, a Christian kingdom.

events.title: The Battle of Stiklestad
events.description: Olaf Haraldsson is killed by a coalition of Norwegian magnates and Danish allies. It is the decisive battle of the Christianisation, and Olaf wins it by losing.

events.title: Olaf canonised as Saint Olaf
events.description: A year after Stiklestad the dead king is declared a saint, his shrine at Nidaros becomes northern Europe's great pilgrimage site, and the dynasty rules in his name.

events.title: Magnus the Good rules Norway and Denmark
events.description: Olaf's son inherits Denmark as well, briefly making Norway the senior partner in a Scandinavian double monarchy.

events.title: Harald Hardrada dies at Stamford Bridge
events.description: The last great Viking king is killed invading England, three weeks before Hastings. His death is the conventional close of the Viking Age.

events.title: Nidaros Cathedral begun
events.description: Building starts over Saint Olaf's grave at Trondheim. It becomes the largest medieval building in Scandinavia and the coronation church of the realm.

events.title: Bergen founded
events.description: Olaf Kyrre establishes a town on the western coast that becomes the kingdom's largest and, for two centuries, its capital.

events.title: Sigurd the Crusader sails for Jerusalem
events.description: A Norwegian king takes sixty ships to the Holy Land, fights alongside Baldwin I and returns overland through Constantinople.

events.title: The civil war era begins
events.description: Sigurd's death opens a century of dynastic war between rival claimants, fought largely because Norwegian succession admitted every royal son, legitimate or not.

events.title: The Archdiocese of Nidaros founded
events.description: A papal legate establishes an archbishopric at Nidaros with authority over Iceland, Greenland, the Faroes, Orkney and the Isle of Man - the church organising a North Atlantic empire the crown had not yet formalised.

events.title: The law of succession restricts the throne
events.description: Magnus Erlingsson is crowned under a new law limiting the succession to one legitimate heir, with the church as arbiter. It does not end the wars but it changes what they are about.

events.title: Sverre Sigurdsson takes the kingdom
events.description: A Faroese priest claiming royal descent defeats Magnus at Fimreite and founds a dynasty, having beaten the church and the aristocracy at once.

events.title: Haakon IV becomes king
events.description: A thirteen-year-old claimant is accepted as king. His long reign ends the civil wars and opens the realm's most confident century.

events.title: Skule Baardsson killed
events.description: The last rival claimant is caught and killed at Nidaros. A hundred and ten years of civil war end, and Norway becomes a stable hereditary monarchy.

events.era_name: The Norwegian realm at its height
events.title: Haakon IV crowned by a papal legate
events.description: Cardinal William of Sabina crowns Haakon at Bergen, settling the legitimacy question that had fuelled the civil wars and recognising Norway as a full European kingdom.

events.era_name: The Norwegian realm at its height
events.title: Trade treaty with Lubeck
events.description: Haakon grants German merchants privileges in Bergen. It secures the grain supply and, over the next century, hands the export trade to the Hanseatic League.

events.era_name: The Norwegian realm at its height
events.title: Greenland submits to the crown
events.description: The Greenland settlements accept Norwegian sovereignty in exchange for guaranteed shipping - a bargain the crown proves unable to keep.

events.era_name: The Norwegian realm at its height
events.title: Iceland accepts Norwegian rule
events.description: Worn down by feuding, the Icelandic chieftains swear allegiance to Haakon IV under the Old Covenant. Norway's Atlantic realm reaches its greatest extent.

events.era_name: The Norwegian realm at its height
events.title: The Hebrides sold to Scotland
events.description: The Treaty of Perth transfers the Hebrides and the Isle of Man to Scotland for a lump sum and an annuity, ending four centuries of Norse rule in the Irish Sea.

events.era_name: The Norwegian realm at its height
events.title: Magnus Lawmender's national code
events.description: A single law code replaces the four regional laws - one of the earliest national legal codes in Europe, and the reason Magnus is remembered as the Lawmender.

events.era_name: The Norwegian realm at its height
events.title: Akershus fortress begun
events.description: Haakon V starts a stone castle at Oslo and moves the centre of royal power east, away from Bergen and towards the Danish and Swedish frontiers.

events.era_name: The Norwegian realm at its height
events.title: Personal union with Sweden
events.description: Haakon V dies without a son and the crown passes to his three-year-old Swedish grandson. Norway is never again ruled by a king who lives there full time.

events.era_name: The Norwegian realm at its height
events.title: The Hanseatic Kontor at Bergen
events.description: German merchants consolidate their Bergen operation into a self-governing enclave that controls the stockfish trade for the next four hundred years.

events.title: The Black Death reaches Bergen
events.description: Plague arrives on an English ship at Bergen and spreads through the whole country within a year, killing somewhere between a third and half the population.

events.title: Farms abandoned and rents collapse
events.description: With so few people left, marginal land goes out of use, land rents fall by two thirds and the Norwegian aristocracy loses the income that sustained it as a separate class.

events.title: The Norwegian nobility thins out
events.description: Plague, falling rents and intermarriage leave too few resident magnates to staff a royal council, so the crown increasingly governs through Danes and Germans.

events.title: The Danish union begins
events.description: Olaf IV inherits both Norway and Denmark. The personal union that follows lasts, in one form or another, for four hundred and thirty-four years.

events.title: The Kalmar Union
events.description: Margaret I unites Denmark, Norway and Sweden under one crown at Kalmar. Norway enters as a kingdom and leaves, much later, as a province.

events.title: The Treaty of Bergen
events.description: A formal act declares Norway and Denmark united under one king in perpetuity, with a council drawn from both. In practice the Danish council dominates.

events.title: Orkney and Shetland pledged to Scotland
events.description: Christian I pawns the northern isles as dowry for his daughter's marriage to James III. The pledge is never redeemed and the islands are lost.

events.title: Stockfish and the timber trade
events.description: Dried cod from Lofoten and timber from the southern fjords become the export economy, both of them shipped and financed by foreigners.

events.title: Sweden leaves the Kalmar Union
events.description: Gustav Vasa breaks Sweden away, leaving Norway alone with Denmark and with far less leverage than it had in a union of three.

events.title: The Reformation imposed
events.description: Christian III makes Lutheranism the state religion, the last Catholic archbishop flees Nidaros, and Norway is declared a Danish province rather than a separate kingdom.

events.title: The Northern Seven Years War reaches Norway
events.description: Swedish forces burn Sarpsborg and lay waste to the eastern districts, the first of a long series of border wars fought on Norwegian ground for Danish purposes.

events.title: Christian IV's northern voyage
events.description: The king sails to Finnmark to assert Danish-Norwegian sovereignty over the Arctic coast against Russian and Swedish claims.

events.title: Oslo burns and becomes Christiania
events.description: Fire destroys Oslo and Christian IV rebuilds it under the walls of Akershus, renaming it after himself. It keeps that name until 1925.

events.title: A standing Norwegian army raised
events.description: Peasant conscription creates a permanent Norwegian army for the first time, which over the next two centuries becomes an unexpected school of national feeling.

events.title: Jamtland and Harjedalen ceded to Sweden
events.description: The Treaty of Bromsebro strips two inland provinces from Norway. The border they created is still the one on the map.

events.title: Trondelag lost and regained
events.description: The Treaty of Roskilde hands Trondelag to Sweden, cutting Norway in half. A local rising and the 1660 Treaty of Copenhagen win it back within two years.

events.title: Bohuslan lost permanently
events.description: The Treaty of Copenhagen confirms the loss of Bohuslan to Sweden, giving Norway its modern southern border.

events.title: The Norwegian Code of Christian V
events.description: A new law code for Norway replaces Magnus Lawmender's, and parts of it remain in force into the twenty-first century.

events.title: Tordenskjold at Dynekilen
events.description: A Norwegian naval officer destroys the Swedish supply fleet at Dynekilen, wrecking Charles XII's invasion and becoming the era's national hero.

events.title: Charles XII killed at Fredriksten
events.description: The Swedish king is shot in the trenches besieging the Norwegian fortress at Halden. The Great Northern War collapses with him.

events.title: Compulsory schooling
events.description: A royal decree requires every child to be taught to read, mainly so they can be confirmed. Norwegian literacy is near universal a century before most of Europe.

events.title: The first census
events.description: Denmark-Norway counts its population: about 723,000 people in Norway, on land that supports almost no towns.

events.title: The Strile War at Bergen
events.description: Coastal farmers march on Bergen against tax collection. It is put down, but it marks the start of organised Norwegian resistance to Copenhagen's fiscal demands.

events.title: Hans Nielsen Hauge and the lay revival
events.description: A farmer's son begins preaching without a licence, building a lay Christian movement that spreads through rural Norway and outlives repeated imprisonment.

events.title: The blockade and the years of hunger
events.description: Britain attacks Copenhagen and blockades Norway, cutting the Danish grain supply. Famine follows, and with it the argument that Norway needs institutions of its own.

events.title: A Norwegian university founded
events.description: After decades of petitioning, Frederick VI allows a university at Christiania. It gives the independence movement its cadre three years before it needs one.

events.title: The Treaty of Kiel
events.description: Defeated as Napoleon's ally, Denmark cedes Norway to the king of Sweden. Norway is handed over without being consulted, and refuses to go quietly.

events.title: The Constitution at Eidsvoll
events.description: A national assembly at Eidsvoll adopts a constitution and elects its own king. It is the most democratic constitution in Europe at the time and it is still in force.

events.title: The Swedish campaign
events.description: A short war ends Norwegian resistance militarily, but Sweden decides the constitution is cheaper to accept than to abolish.

events.title: The Convention of Moss
events.description: Norway accepts the Swedish king and keeps the Eidsvoll constitution. It enters the union as a state with its own parliament, laws and army.

events.title: The Storting abolishes noble privilege
events.description: Parliament votes down the remaining aristocratic titles over royal objection, and Norway becomes a country of farmers and officials with no landed nobility.

events.title: The Restauration sails for New York
events.description: Fifty-two people leave Stavanger for America on a small sloop, beginning an emigration that eventually takes more than 800,000 Norwegians - proportionally second only to Ireland.

events.title: Local self-government
events.description: The Formannskapslov gives every municipality an elected council. It builds the habit of self-rule from the parish upwards.

events.title: The first railway opens
events.description: A line runs from Christiania to Eidsvoll, the start of a network that is still fighting the terrain a century and a half later.

events.title: Ibsen, Bjornson and the national romantics
events.description: A generation of writers, painters and folk-tale collectors builds a Norwegian cultural identity, giving the political movement something to be about.

events.title: Sami land rights curtailed
events.description: The state intensifies a policy of Norwegianisation, restricting Sami and Kven language use in schools and church and tying land rights to Norwegian speech.

events.title: The Storting meets annually
events.description: Parliament wins the right to sit every year rather than every third year, which turns it from an event into a government.

events.title: A Doll's House
events.description: Ibsen's play is published in Copenhagen and scandalises Europe. Norwegian literature becomes, briefly, the most talked-about in the world.

events.title: Parliamentarism established
events.description: After a constitutional crisis and an impeachment, the king accepts that governments must hold the confidence of the Storting. Norway's first political parties form the same year.

events.title: Munch paints The Scream
events.description: Edvard Munch finishes the first version of The Scream in Berlin, and Norwegian art acquires its single most reproduced image.

events.title: Nansen returns from the Arctic drift
events.description: Fridtjof Nansen comes back from three years in the ice, having reached a record northern latitude and made polar exploration a Norwegian national project.

events.title: Universal male suffrage
events.description: The property qualification is abolished for men. Norway becomes one of the first countries in Europe where every adult man can vote.

events.title: The Storting dissolves the union
events.description: Parliament declares the Swedish king has ceased to function as king of Norway. A referendum backs it 368,208 to 184, and Sweden lets it go without a war.

events.title: Haakon VII takes the throne
events.description: A Danish prince is elected king by referendum, takes a Norwegian regnal name and a Norwegian-speaking household, and reigns for fifty-two years.

events.title: Hydroelectric industry takes off
events.description: Cheap waterfall power draws electrochemical industry to the fjords, and Norsk Hydro is founded to fix nitrogen for fertiliser.

events.title: The Concession Laws
events.description: Parliament restricts foreign ownership of waterfalls and mines, establishing early the principle that natural resources belong to the nation.

events.title: Amundsen reaches the South Pole
events.description: Roald Amundsen's party arrives at the pole thirty-four days before Scott, using dogs, skis and a route nobody had tried.

events.title: Women get the vote
events.description: Norway grants full female suffrage, the first sovereign state in Europe to do so through its own parliament.

events.title: The neutral ally
events.description: Norway stays out of the war but charters its merchant fleet to Britain. Half the fleet and about two thousand sailors are lost to submarines.

events.title: The Svalbard Treaty
events.description: Norway gains sovereignty over Svalbard on condition that all signatories keep equal rights to fish, hunt and mine there. Russia still uses that clause.

events.title: Christiania becomes Oslo again
events.description: The capital drops its Danish royal name and takes back the medieval one.

events.title: Sigrid Undset wins the Nobel Prize
events.description: The second Norwegian laureate in literature is honoured for her medieval trilogy, written while the country was arguing about what its past had been.

events.title: Labour takes power
events.description: Johan Nygaardsvold forms a Labour government on a crisis agreement with the farmers, beginning four decades of social democratic dominance.

events.title: Germany invades
events.description: Operation Weserubung lands at seven points at once. The cruiser Blucher is sunk in the Oslofjord, which buys the king and the government the hours they need to escape.

events.title: The battles for Narvik
events.description: Allied and Norwegian forces retake Narvik in the first German ground defeat of the war, then abandon it when France collapses.

events.title: The king refuses and leaves
events.description: Haakon VII rejects a German demand to appoint Quisling, telling the government he will abdicate rather than comply, and sails for London with the gold reserves.

events.title: Quisling installed
events.description: Vidkun Quisling is made minister-president of a collaborationist government. His name has already entered English as a word for traitor.

events.title: The heavy water sabotage
events.description: Norwegian commandos destroy the heavy water plant at Vemork, then sink the ferry carrying the remaining stock, setting back the German nuclear programme.

events.title: Finnmark burned
events.description: Retreating German forces destroy almost every building in Finnmark and northern Troms and deport 50,000 people. The Red Army liberates Kirkenes the same month.

events.title: Liberation
events.description: German forces in Norway surrender. The king returns on 7 June, five years to the day after he left.

events.title: Quisling executed
events.description: Quisling is shot at Akershus after a treason trial. Some 46,000 people are convicted in the purge that follows.

events.title: Trygve Lie becomes UN Secretary-General
events.description: Norway's foreign minister takes the first Secretary-Generalship, setting the template for a small state buying influence through international institutions.

events.title: Norway joins NATO
events.description: After a Nordic defence pact fails, Norway abandons neutrality and becomes a founding NATO member - with a self-imposed ban on foreign bases in peacetime.

events.title: The Nordic Council founded
events.description: Norway helps set up a standing Nordic parliamentary body, and a passport union follows in 1954.

events.title: EFTA and the trade question
events.description: Norway joins the European Free Trade Association rather than the Common Market, choosing access without membership - a pattern it never really leaves.

events.title: Phillips asks for a licence
events.description: An American company applies to explore the Norwegian shelf. Nobody in government believes there is oil there, and the reply is that Norway will not grant a monopoly.

events.title: The shelf divided
events.description: Agreements with Britain and Denmark split the North Sea along the median line, before anyone knows what is under it. Norway's share turns out to include most of the oil.

events.title: Ekofisk found
events.description: Phillips strikes oil at Ekofisk on what was meant to be its last well. It is one of the largest offshore fields ever found and it changes the country.

events.title: The ten oil commandments
events.description: Parliament adopts principles for the petroleum industry: national control, a state company, and the revenue used to benefit the whole society. This is why the money was not wasted.

events.title: The first EC referendum says no
events.description: Voters reject membership of the European Communities 53.5 to 46.5, splitting the country between the cities and the coast and districts. The government falls.

events.title: Statoil founded
events.description: A wholly state-owned oil company is created to hold Norway's share of the fields and to build the expertise to operate them.

events.title: The Bravo blowout
events.description: A well on Ekofisk blows out and spills for eight days, the North Sea's first major oil accident, and the reason the safety regime got teeth.

events.title: The Alta dam conflict
events.description: Mass civil disobedience against a hydro dam on the Alta river becomes the decisive Sami political mobilisation. The dam is built; the movement wins everything after it.

events.title: Alexander Kielland capsizes
events.description: An accommodation platform overturns in the North Sea and 123 men die, the worst disaster in Norwegian offshore history.

events.title: Gro Harlem Brundtland becomes prime minister
events.description: Norway's first woman prime minister takes office at forty-one. Her 1986 cabinet is eight women out of eighteen, which was then unheard of anywhere.

events.title: The Brundtland Report
events.description: A UN commission chaired by Brundtland publishes Our Common Future and puts the phrase sustainable development into general use.

events.title: The Sami Parliament opens
events.description: An elected Sami assembly is established at Karasjok, eight years after Alta, with authority over Sami language, culture and education.

events.title: The oil fund created
events.description: Parliament establishes what becomes the Government Pension Fund Global to hold petroleum revenue offshore. The first deposit is made in 1996.

events.title: The Oslo Accords negotiated
events.description: Norwegian diplomats broker secret Israeli-Palestinian talks in Oslo, the high point of the small-state mediation role.

events.title: The Lillehammer Olympics
events.description: The Winter Games are held in a town of 25,000. Norway finishes second in the medal table and the event is still cited as the model for a small host.

events.title: The second EU referendum says no
events.description: Voters reject EU membership again, 52.2 to 47.8. Norway joins the European Economic Area instead and takes the rules without the vote.

events.title: Snohvit and the move north
events.description: Gas development starts in the Barents Sea, pushing the industry into Arctic waters and reopening the boundary question with Russia.

events.title: Ethical guidelines for the fund
events.description: The oil fund adopts exclusion criteria and starts divesting from weapons, tobacco and serious environmental damage, making it an instrument of policy as well as savings.

events.title: The Barents Sea boundary settled
events.description: Norway and Russia agree a maritime border after forty years of dispute, dividing 175,000 square kilometres of the Barents Sea almost equally.

events.title: The Oslo and Utoya attacks
events.description: A far-right terrorist bombs the government quarter and then shoots 69 people, most of them teenagers, at a Labour youth camp on Utoya. Seventy-seven die in all.

events.title: A conservative government
events.description: Erna Solberg wins on a platform of tax cuts and, later, restraint in spending the oil fund. She governs for eight years.

events.title: The fund passes ten trillion kroner
events.description: The oil fund crosses ten trillion kroner, roughly triple annual GDP, and becomes the largest sovereign wealth fund in the world.

events.title: The Fosen wind judgment
events.description: The Supreme Court rules that wind turbines on Fosen violate Sami reindeer herders' rights under international law, setting the energy transition against indigenous rights.

events.title: Europe's largest gas supplier
events.description: With Russian pipeline gas cut off, Norway becomes the European Union's biggest supplier and records extraordinary revenues from a war it is not fighting.

events.title: Electric cars pass ninety per cent
events.description: Battery electric vehicles take more than nine in ten new car sales, the highest share anywhere, funded by tax exemptions paid for out of petroleum revenue.
